2027-03-11.title: Thursday of the Fourth Week of Lent
readings: Turn from your fierce wrath; change your mind and do not bring disaster on your people
Remember us, O Lord, as you favor your people
Your accuser is Moses, on whom you have set your hope
2027-03-11.alt: Lenten weekday. The Gloria and the Alleluia are omitted throughout Lent. Liturgical colour: violet.
2027-03-11.verse: You search the scriptures because you think that in them you have eternal life; and it is they that testify on my behalf. Yet you refuse to come to me to have life.
theo: At the foot of Sinai, only weeks after the covenant, the people grow tired of waiting for Moses and make a calf of gold. God says to Moses: “Go down at once! Your people… have acted perversely.” They have “cast for themselves an image of a calf” and said, “These are your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt!” The Psalm puts it sharply: “They exchanged the glory of God for the image of an ox that eats grass.” Then God tests Moses: “Now let me alone, so that my wrath may burn hot against them… and of you I will make a great nation.” Moses refuses the offer. He stands, as the Psalm says, “in the breach,” between God and the people, and pleads: they are your people, whom you brought out of Egypt; what will the nations say? “Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, your servants.” And “the LORD changed his mind about the disaster that he planned to bring on his people.” God does not change like a moody human being; Scripture speaks in human terms to show that he has willed to let the prayer of his friends shape history. Moses is the great intercessor, and a figure of Christ, who “always lives to make intercession” for us.

In the Gospel Jesus calls witnesses, as in a court. John the Baptist testified: he was “a burning and shining lamp.” The works the Father gave Jesus to do testify. The Father himself testifies. And the Scriptures testify: “You search the scriptures because you think that in them you have eternal life; and it is they that testify on my behalf. Yet you refuse to come to me to have life.” It is possible to know the Bible well and still miss the Person to whom it points. Then a surprise: “Your accuser is Moses, on whom you have set your hope… he wrote about me.” The same Moses who once pleaded for a sinful people now bears witness to Jesus. Jesus is speaking to the religious leaders who opposed him, not condemning the Jewish people; the Church received from Israel the Scriptures, the covenants and the promises, and reads Moses with deep reverence. The question is for us too: do we read the Scriptures in order to come to Christ? Lent invites us to put away our own golden calves, the things we worship instead of God, and to come to the One of whom the whole of Scripture speaks.
outline: Ask: what do people today put in God's place?
Exchanging God's glory for an idol.
Reading the Bible to come to Christ.
“Remember us, O Lord, as you favor your people.”
live: Ask honestly: what do I trust more than God? Give it back to him today.
Pray today, by name, for someone who has turned away from God.
2027-03-11.prayer: Lord God, you listened to the prayer of Moses and spared your people. Free us from every golden calf, and give us hearts that intercede for others. Open our minds to understand the Scriptures, that we may come to your Son and have life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: Christ our High Priest, the true Moses, stands between God and us and offers himself for sinners. At every Mass his sacrifice is made present, and his intercession is our hope.

quick: Israel made a golden calf; Moses interceded and God spared them.
Jesus calls witnesses: John, his works, the Father and the Scriptures.
We read the Scriptures in order to come to Christ and have life.
2027-03-11.action: Pray by name for someone who has wandered from God.
2027-03-11.question: What golden calf is taking God's place in my life?

family.explain: When God's people made a golden statue and worshipped it, Moses prayed hard for them, and God forgave them. Moses was like a bridge between God and the people. Jesus is our bridge too, and we can pray for others like Moses did.
family.intention: We pray for people who have stopped praying or going to church.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anything we love more than God? What can we do about it this Lent?”

illus: A mother in Changanassery prayed for her son for twenty-two years after he stopped going to church. Every night, before sleeping, she said his name at the crucifix. When at last he returned to confession, the priest asked what had brought him back. He said: I do not know. Then he paused and said: yes, I know. My mother never stopped standing between me and the door.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you always live to intercede for us. Teach us to stand in the breach for others. Amen.
share: They have cast for themselves an image of a calf (Exodus 32:8). What do I worship in place of God?
But Moses implored the LORD his God (Exodus 32:11). For whom am I being asked to plead?
Yet you refuse to come to me to have life (John 5:40). Do I read Scripture to meet Christ?
pm.resp: Remember us, O Lord, as you favor your people.
interc: For those who have turned to idols of money, power or pleasure, that they may return.
For parents praying for children who have left the faith.
For priests, that they may stand before God for their people.
For Christians and Jews, that we may read the Scriptures with reverence and grow in friendship.
For our group, that we may become faithful intercessors.
pm.close: Father, you heard Moses and spared your people. Hear our prayer through Christ, our High Priest. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, at the foot of Mount Sinai the people grew impatient and made a golden calf. They exchanged the glory of God for the image of an ox that eats grass, as the Psalm says. We laugh at them, but we do the same: we put money, success, our phones or our pride in the place of God.

God says to Moses: let me alone… and of you I will make a great nation. But Moses will not leave his people. He pleads: O LORD, why does your wrath burn hot against your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt? (Exodus 32:11). Remember Abraham, Isaac and Israel. And God spares them. That is the power of intercession.

Moses points to Jesus, who stands between God and us, and always lives to make intercession for us. In the Gospel Jesus says: you search the scriptures because you think that in them you have eternal life; and it is they that testify on my behalf. Yet you refuse to come to me to have life (John 5:39–40). The Bible is not just a book to study. It is a road to a Person.
This Lent, let us break our golden calves. Let us pray for someone who has wandered, as Moses prayed, as many mothers pray. And let us open the Scriptures every day to meet Jesus there. Amen.
kids: Children, God's people made a golden statue of a calf and prayed to it instead of to God. Moses prayed for them and God forgave them. Let us pray today for someone we love, like Moses did.

intro: Theme: “It is they that testify on my behalf.”
The golden calf, Moses in the breach, and the Scriptures that lead us to Christ.

q: They exchanged the glory of God for the image of an ox that eats grass.
Little children, keep yourselves from idols.
points.apply: Fast this week from the thing that most often takes God's place in your day.

q: But Moses implored the LORD his God, and said, “O LORD, why does your wrath burn hot against your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt with great power and with a mighty hand?
Consequently he is able for all time to save those who approach God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them.
points.apply: Write the names of three people far from God and pray for them every day until Easter.

q: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet.
You search the scriptures because you think that in them you have eternal life; and it is they that testify on my behalf. Yet you refuse to come to me to have life.
points.apply: Read the Gospel of the day each morning this week, and end with a short prayer to Jesus.

concl: God's people fell into idolatry, and Moses' prayer saved them.
Christ is the eternal intercessor, and all the Scriptures lead to him.
2027-03-11.resolve: Pray daily for three people far from God until Easter.
